title: The four tabs All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed work in every display
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-352 led by Esther Howard):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose a customer (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
  6. Put three of your work orders in different statuses (open each one and change its status with the status control on the work order page):
    • one left in Estimate (e.g. S1-352), one moved to Approved (e.g. S1-702), one moved to Complete (e.g. S1-689). All three led by Esther Howard.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders and stay in List.
  2. Click each tab in turn: All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed. For each tab write down which of your three work orders appear.
  3. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (in the design its tooltip reads "By Lead Tech").
  4. Click each tab in turn again and write down which of your three work orders appear under Esther Howard.
  5. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  6. Click each tab in turn again and write down which of your three work orders appear in Esther Howard's column.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • All four tabs (All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed) are shown in every display.
  • Each tab shows the same work orders in List, Tech View and Board View. With the example data: All shows 3 (S1-352, S1-702, S1-689), Work Orders shows S1-702, Estimates shows S1-352, Completed shows S1-689.
  • This case does not check which tab opens first: the default tab was taken out of scope and stays as production has it today.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), Feature Overview, Key Decisions, read 8 Oct 2026. PO decision Chris Ward, PRD footer comment 25 Sep 2026 ("The default-tab change is out too"). Review Decisions 853901313 DR-33.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • Feature Overview: “The existing filter views (the tabs on the left — All, Work Orders, Estimates, Completed) and the filter bar (search, status, assigned to me, and so on) apply the same way in every display option.”
  • Key Decisions: “Permissions. Work Orders view permits viewing all four filter tabs and reordering technician groups/columns.”
